description: Two-panel conceptual schematic (no axes, no scale bar, no numeric data printed) illustrating how intergranular κ-carbides alter cyclic slip behaviour in Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel. Both panels share the same construction: a vertical red line labelled "GB" (grain boundary) separates a left grain captioned "Soft-oriented grain" in red from a right grain captioned "Hard-oriented grain" in blue. (a) is headed "Absence of intergranular κ-carbides": several dashed blue lines labelled "Planar slip bands", decorated with T-shaped dislocation symbols, run across both grains and cross the GB unobstructed, so dislocations transfer freely from the soft- into the hard-oriented grain. (b) is headed "Presence of intergranular κ-carbides": four yellow barrel-shaped particles sit on the GB, annotated "Intergranular κ-carbides" with orange arrows; the slip bands now terminate at these particles and magenta arrows mark "Dislocation pile-ups" where dislocations accumulate against the boundary. Together the panels argue that a clean grain boundary permits slip transfer and suppresses localization, whereas intergranular κ-carbides block slip, generate pile-ups and local stress concentrations, promoting early strain localization and crack initiation. The caption states the schematic shows Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys; the citing text ties (a) to the 550-6 and (b) to the 650-6 condition.

observations.observation: Both panels use a vertical red line labelled 'GB' as the grain boundary, with the left grain labelled 'Soft-oriented grain' (red text) and the right grain 'Hard-oriented grain' (blue text).
In panel (a) the dashed blue lines carrying T-shaped dislocation symbols are labelled 'Planar slip bands' and run continuously across the GB into the adjacent grain.
Panel (a) is titled 'Absence of intergranular κ-carbides' and shows no precipitate on the GB line.
Panel (b) is titled 'Presence of intergranular κ-carbides' and shows four yellow barrel-shaped particles located on the red GB line, annotated 'Intergranular κ-carbides' with orange arrows.
In panel (b) the slip bands terminate at the GB particles and magenta arrows label 'Dislocation pile-ups', indicating blocked dislocation motion and accumulation at the boundary.
Neither panel contains axes, scale bars, legends or printed numerical values; the figure is purely qualitative.
The caption states the figure is a schematic diagram showing the impact of the absence (a) and presence (b) of intergranular κ-carbides on the cyclic deformation behaviour of Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys.

The citing text states that in the 550-6 sample, which has a homogeneous intragranular κ-carbide distribution and an absence of intergranular κ-carbides, dislocation slip transfer is facilitated and localization is suppressed (corresponds to panel (a)).

The citing text states that in the 650-6 sample severe intergranular κ-carbides impede dislocation slip at grain boundaries, causing severe dislocation pile-ups, local stress concentrations and accelerated strain localization leading to premature crack initiation and failure (corresponds to panel (b)).
The citing text reports the fatigue-life ranking at high stress amplitudes as 550-6 best, 600-6 intermediate and 650-6 poorest, tracking the increasing severity of intergranular precipitation.

The citing text states that the detrimental grain-boundary effect of intergranular κ-carbides offsets the size benefit at low stress amplitudes and also degrades fatigue resistance at high stress amplitudes by the same mechanism.

subfigures.description: Schematic headed 'Absence of intergranular κ-carbides'. A red vertical GB line divides a 'Soft-oriented grain' (red, left) from a 'Hard-oriented grain' (blue, right). Dashed blue lines labelled 'Planar slip bands' with T-shaped dislocation symbols traverse both grains and cross the GB without obstruction, depicting unobstructed dislocation slip transfer.

Schematic headed 'Presence of intergranular κ-carbides'. Same GB/grain colour convention, but four yellow barrel-shaped intergranular κ-carbide particles lie along the red GB line (orange arrow labels 'Intergranular κ-carbides'). Slip bands stop at the particles and magenta arrows label 'Dislocation pile-ups' against the boundary, depicting blocked slip and local stress concentration.

unreadable_items: The '(a)' / '(b)' panel letters are not clearly printed inside the two images (only a faint cropped mark at the top of the first panel); panel assignment follows the caption ordering.
No sample condition labels (e.g. 550-6, 650-6) are printed on either panel; they are only given in the citing text.
